Description:en: A subset of therapeutic foods, ready-to-use therapeutic foods (RUTFs), are energy-dense, micro nutrient-enriched pastes that have a nutritional profile similar to the traditional F-100 milk-based diet used in inpatient therapeutic feeding programs and are often made of peanuts, oil, sugar and milk powder.
Describes a substance used to feed children.
F-75 is considered the "starter" formula that delivers 75kcal/100ml.
Designed and marketed for feeding to babies born before term, usually prepared for cup-feeding from powder (mixed with water).
F-100 is considered the "catch-up" formula that delivers 100kcal/100ml.
ReSoMal (oral rehydration salts or ORS for severely malnourished children) is used in in-patient centres for the treatment of children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM).

FBFs are blends of partially precooked and milled cereals, soya, beans, pulses fortified with micro-nutrients (vitamins and minerals). Special formulations may contain vegetable oil or milk powder. Corn Soya Blend (CSB) is the main blended flours.
A fortified blended flour specifically made from corn and soy blend fortified with micronutrients
Nutrition supplements that are in liquid formulations
Multiple micro-nutrients are only needed in very small quantities but are essential for normal physiological function, growth and development.
